days.title: Day 21 – Advanced Form Techniques
days.definition: Advanced HTML form features include complex validation, custom controls, accessibility enhancements, and integration with JavaScript for dynamic behavior.

explanation.main: Intermediate form techniques go beyond basic inputs to create professional, user-friendly forms.
key_points: HTML5 introduced advanced input types with built-in validation
Form accessibility is crucial for inclusive design
Fieldset and legend elements group related form controls
Custom validation messages improve user experience
Form data can be processed client-side before submission

days.real_world_example: Advanced forms are used in banking applications for secure transactions, e-commerce checkout processes with multiple steps, job application portals with file uploads, survey platforms with conditional logic, and CRM systems with complex data entry requirements.

quiz.question: Which HTML5 element provides pre-defined options for an input field?
quiz.reasoning: The <datalist> element provides a list of pre-defined options for an <input> element. (Reference: W3Schools Datalist)

quiz.question: How do you allow multiple file uploads?
quiz.reasoning: The 'multiple' attribute allows users to select multiple files. (Reference: W3Schools Input File)

quiz.question: What does the pattern attribute do?
quiz.reasoning: The pattern attribute specifies a regular expression for input validation. (Reference: W3Schools Input Pattern)

quiz.question: Which element groups related form controls?
quiz.reasoning: <fieldset> groups related elements in a form. (Reference: W3Schools Fieldset)

quiz.question: How do you show validation errors to users?
quiz.reasoning: The :invalid CSS pseudo-class selects form elements with invalid values. (Reference: W3Schools :invalid)

days.title: Day 22 – HTML APIs Introduction
days.definition: HTML APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) are built-in browser features that enable web pages to interact with device hardware, browser capabilities, and user data.

explanation.main: HTML5 introduced powerful APIs that extend web functionality beyond traditional pages.
key_points: Web Storage API provides client-side data storage
Geolocation API accesses user's location (with permission)
Drag and Drop API enables interactive element movement
Web Workers run scripts in background threads
Page Visibility API detects when page is visible

interactive_tasks: Create a note-taking app using localStorage
Build a drag-and-drop file upload interface
Implement a location-based weather widget

quiz.question: Which API provides client-side storage that persists after browser closes?
quiz.reasoning: localStorage provides persistent storage that survives browser sessions. (Reference: W3Schools localStorage)

quiz.question: What attribute makes an element draggable?
quiz.reasoning: The draggable attribute set to true enables drag functionality. (Reference: W3Schools Draggable)

quiz.question: Which event prevents default to allow dropping?
quiz.reasoning: Calling preventDefault() on dragover event allows drop. (Reference: W3Schools Drag and Drop)

quiz.question: How do you check if geolocation is available?
quiz.reasoning: navigator.geolocation checks for geolocation support. (Reference: W3Schools Geolocation)

quiz.question: What does the Page Visibility API detect?
quiz.reasoning: Page Visibility API detects when a tab becomes visible or hidden. (Reference: MDN Page Visibility API)

days.title: Day 23 – Canvas and Graphics
days.definition: HTML Canvas element provides a drawing surface for creating dynamic, scriptable graphics, charts, animations, and image processing directly in the browser.

explanation.main: Canvas enables pixel-based graphics rendering through JavaScript.
key_points: Canvas is resolution-dependent bitmap drawing surface
Requires JavaScript to draw anything
Supports 2D and 3D (WebGL) rendering contexts
Ideal for games, data visualization, and image editing
Can export canvas content as images

quiz.question: How do you get the drawing context for 2D?
quiz.reasoning: getContext('2d') returns the 2D rendering context. (Reference: W3Schools Canvas getContext)

quiz.question: Which method draws a rectangle?
quiz.reasoning: fillRect() draws a filled rectangle. (Reference: W3Schools fillRect)

quiz.question: How do you start a new path?
quiz.reasoning: beginPath() begins a new path. (Reference: W3Schools beginPath)

quiz.question: Which method exports canvas as image URL?
quiz.reasoning: toDataURL() returns a data URL containing image representation. (Reference: W3Schools toDataURL)

quiz.question: What does requestAnimationFrame() do?
quiz.reasoning: requestAnimationFrame() optimizes animations for smooth rendering. (Reference: W3Schools requestAnimationFrame)

days.title: Day 24 – SVG in HTML
days.definition: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is an XML-based markup language for describing two-dimensional vector graphics that scale without quality loss.

explanation.main: SVG provides resolution-independent graphics directly in HTML.
key_points: SVG graphics are scalable without pixelation
Defined using XML tags within HTML
Can be styled with CSS and animated
Accessible and search engine friendly
Smaller file sizes for simple graphics

quiz.question: What does SVG stand for?
quiz.reasoning: SVG stands for Scalable Vector Graphics. (Reference: W3Schools SVG)

quiz.question: How do you make SVG responsive?
quiz.reasoning: Setting width='100%' and viewBox attribute makes SVG responsive. (Reference: W3Schools SVG ViewBox)

quiz.question: Which attribute defines SVG fill color?
quiz.reasoning: The fill attribute defines the color inside an SVG element. (Reference: W3Schools SVG Fill)

quiz.question: How can SVG be animated?
quiz.reasoning: SVG can be animated using CSS, SMIL, or JavaScript. (Reference: W3Schools SVG Animation)

Responsive table designs for mobile
Sorting and filtering capabilities
Fixed headers for large datasets

days.title: Day 26 – Web Components Basics
days.definition: Web Components are a set of web platform APIs that allow you to create reusable custom HTML elements with encapsulated functionality and styling.

explanation.main: Web Components enable building reusable UI components.
key_points: Custom Elements: Define new HTML tags
Shadow DOM: Encapsulated styling and markup
HTML Templates: Reusable markup structures
ES Modules: Component importing system
Works across modern browsers without frameworks

quiz.question: What does Shadow DOM provide?
quiz.reasoning: Shadow DOM provides style and markup encapsulation. (Reference: MDN Shadow DOM)

quiz.question: Which lifecycle method is called when element is added to DOM?
quiz.reasoning: connectedCallback() is called when element is connected to DOM. (Reference: MDN connectedCallback)

days.title: Day 27 – Performance Optimization
days.definition: HTML performance optimization involves techniques to make web pages load faster, use less bandwidth, and provide better user experience through efficient markup and resource management.

explanation.main: Optimizing HTML improves site speed and user experience.
key_points: Minimal and semantic markup reduces file size
Efficient resource loading with lazy loading
Proper use of caching headers and CDNs
Optimized images and media delivery
Critical rendering path optimization

days.definition: HTML Internationalization (i18n) involves creating web content that can be easily adapted to different languages and regions without engineering changes.

explanation.main: Internationalization makes websites accessible to global audiences.
key_points: lang attribute specifies content language
dir attribute controls text direction
Unicode (UTF-8) supports all languages
Localization adapts content for specific regions
Accessibility considerations for multilingual users

quiz.question: Which attribute specifies content language?
quiz.reasoning: The lang attribute specifies the language of element content. (Reference: W3Schools Lang)

quiz.question: What does dir="rtl" do?
quiz.reasoning: dir="rtl" sets right-to-left text direction for languages like Arabic. (Reference: W3Schools Dir)

quiz.question: Which charset supports all languages?
quiz.reasoning: UTF-8 supports all Unicode characters and languages. (Reference: W3Schools UTF-8)

quiz.question: What is the purpose of <time datetime>?
quiz.reasoning: datetime attribute provides machine-readable date/time. (Reference: W3Schools Time)

quiz.question: How to indicate language changes within page?
quiz.reasoning: Use lang attribute on specific elements for language changes within page. (Reference: MDN Language Tags)

explanation.main: Accessibility creates inclusive web experiences for all users.
key_points: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) standards
ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes
Keyboard navigation and focus management
Screen reader compatibility
Color contrast and text readability

quiz.question: What does WCAG stand for?
quiz.reasoning: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. (Reference: W3C WCAG)

quiz.question: Which ARIA attribute indicates dynamic content updates?
quiz.reasoning: aria-live indicates live region for dynamic content. (Reference: MDN aria-live)

quiz.question: What is the minimum color contrast ratio for normal text?
quiz.reasoning: WCAG requires 4.5:1 contrast for normal text. (Reference: WCAG Contrast)

quiz.question: How to make custom div clickable via keyboard?
quiz.reasoning: Use tabindex="0" or better, use <button> element. (Reference: MDN Keyboard Accessibility)

quiz.question: What does role="navigation" do?
quiz.reasoning: role="navigation" identifies navigation landmarks for screen readers. (Reference: MDN ARIA Roles)
